clue.text: Stress two different points about unusual mishap

indicators.note: the two compass points sit about, that is around, the rearranged letters

parts.note: E and S are two different compass points, east and south

indicators.note: an unusual version of the word mishap has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stresses a couple of points about a strange accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges MISHAP into MPHASI, and 'about' puts E and S around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress laid on a word or idea is the weight or importance given to it, a synonym.

clue.text: Two consecutive letters supporting Tom's initial work

parts.note: E and F follow each other in the alphabet
to be for something is to support it

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter, here of Tom

explanation.surface: A pair of letters back up Tom's first piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the letters EF sit on top of FOR and T, which 'supporting' suits as a picture too.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort and work both mean exertion put into a task, a synonym.

clue.text: Stop taking responsibility for what traffic policeman does

parts.note: a full stop is a point in punctuation
a duty is a responsibility one must carry out

explanation.surface: Someone stops taking charge of what a traffic officer does.
explanation.walkthrough: Point duty is the British term for a police officer standing at a junction directing traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Point duty is the job of a constable posted at a crossroads to direct the cars, the descriptive phrase.

clue.text: A long letter

parts.note: to long for something is to have an itch for it

explanation.surface: Someone writes a lengthy letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective describing the letter, but it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the spoken name of the eighth letter of the alphabet, H.

clue.text: Properly arranged in sequence that's correct

explanation.surface: Things are set out properly, in an approved sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is about arrangement; the second is the meeting-room sense, as when a chair rules a point acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both placed in the right series and, of a procedure, permissible under the rules.

clue.text: At university, a specified day for revision

parts.note: a student is up at university while in residence
a date is a day fixed for something

explanation.surface: A student sets a day aside for revising for exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' suggests exam study, but it means a new version brought up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: A revision is a newer version of something, the sense of an amended edition.

clue.text: Publicity for the movement

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons
motion is another word for movement

explanation.surface: A campaign seeks publicity for a political movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion is advertising and publicity used to push a product or cause, a synonym.

clue.text: Stand-offish American clot turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a clot is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: An unfriendly American idiot arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses FOOL to LOOF, read upwards in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stand-offish keeps distant and reserved, the same as being aloof.

clue.text: Ordinary person may never broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: An average person may never appear on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests radio or television, but it is the anagram signal for MAY NEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An everyman is the typical common individual, standing for people in general.

clue.text: Novels about Richard I's conflict

indicators.note: the novels word goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: novels are works of fiction
R is an abbreviation for the name Richard

explanation.surface: Stories about King Richard the First tell of his wars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R and I inside FICTION, after the F.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction is disagreement and clashing between people, a synonym for conflict.

clue.text: Blue Missouri flower

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Missouri
a rose is a flower

explanation.surface: A blue flower grows in Missouri.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour describing the flower, but it means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel blue is to be gloomy and sullen, the same as morose.

clue.text: Talk boastfully and quietly catch one's breath

parts.note: to gas is to talk idly or boastfully
p, for piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone brags, then softly stops for air.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to draw in breath sharply, a synonym of catching one's breath.

clue.text: Gag such a dreadful person, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: a wretch is a miserable or despicable person

explanation.surface: Someone tells a horrible person to shut up.
explanation.walkthrough: The W of WRETCH is silent, so it is said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to heave as if about to vomit, a synonym.

clue.text: Fierce lady takes on crafty insect

parts.note: a dragon is a fierce, intimidating woman
fly is British slang for knowing or crafty

explanation.surface: A formidable woman takes on a cunning bug.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a long-bodied flying insect with two pairs of wings, an example.

clue.text: Very big bottom on small person

parts.note: bum is British slang for the bottom

indicators.note: made small, the word person is cut down to its abbreviated form

parts.note: the full word person, shortened

explanation.surface: A huge backside sits on a little person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' shortens PERSON to PER; 'on' places BUM before it in the across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumper crop or harvest is an exceptionally large one, so the word means huge.

clue.text: Traveller who is not much of a contributor to team effort

definitions.text: who is not much of a contributor to team effort

explanation.surface: A traveller is called a freeloader in the team.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is the figurative sense of someone carried along by colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means someone riding in a vehicle and also a team member who coasts while others do the work.

clue.text: Plant providing proper upper class note

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper
U is the British abbreviation for upper class
la is a note in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A plant offers a prim, posh musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a garden plant such as the primrose or cowslip, an example of a plant.

clue.text: More expensive surroundings are disturbing

parts.note: prices that are up are higher than before
a setting is the surroundings of something

explanation.surface: Pricier surroundings are troubling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upsetting causes distress, the same as disturbing.

clue.text: Team game in which the French thwart Spain

parts.note: la is a French word for the
to cross someone is to thwart them
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: In a sport, the French frustrate the Spanish side.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a team sport played with netted sticks, an example of a team game.

clue.text: Lays out amount needed for border plant

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the word lays are put out of their order

parts.note: a sum is an amount

explanation.surface: A gardener sets out the money needed for an edging plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LAYS into ALYS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a low flowering plant often used to edge flowerbeds, an example.

clue.text: Come across to lift bucket down

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the word puts its letters from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to bucket down is British for to rain heavily, to teem

explanation.surface: Someone tries to raise a bucket and lower it again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lift' turns TEEM upwards in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across someone is to encounter them, a synonym.

clue.text: Stop sounding foreign

indicators.note: sounding signals that the word is heard, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: Finnish, from Finland, is one example of foreign

explanation.surface: Someone tells an outsider to quit sounding so foreign.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition by example is fair: Finnish is one kind of foreign.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish is to come to an end, a synonym of stop.

clue.text: The most healthy are apt to try

parts.note: fit means suitable or apt
to test something is to try it

explanation.surface: The healthiest people are ready to give it a go.
explanation.definitionFit: Fittest is the superlative of fit, meaning in the best physical condition.

clue.text: Prince is wary about the British leader

indicators.note: the word for wary goes about, around, the other letter

parts.note: alert means watchful and wary

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of British

explanation.surface: A prince is cautious about the leader of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts B inside ALERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's consort, an example of a prince.

clue.text: Introduce again the engineers in attendance

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers of the British Army
to be present is to be in attendance

explanation.surface: Someone presents the engineers again while they are there.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyphenated, the answer means to present again, distinct from the usual sense of stand for.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-present is to bring something forward once more, the definition taken literally.

clue.text: Small ponds are a gamble single-masted craft capsize

indicators.note: in a down clue, capsizing turns the boat upside down, so its letters are read upwards

parts.note: a sloop is a sailing boat with one mast

explanation.surface: Small ponds are risky places to sail a little boat that might overturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are a gamble' adds the football pools, the British betting on match results, as a second sense; 'capsize' reverses SLOOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Pools are small areas of still water, the same as small ponds.

clue.text: Sex appeal in a small girl is essential

indicators.note: in signals one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: Val is a shortened girl's name, from Valerie
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A little girl's charm is vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' means the name is a short form, not that the girl is young.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vital is indispensable, a synonym of essential.

clue.text: First of all, vin ordinaire doesn't kill alcoholics stronger liquor is needed

indicators.note: first of all asks for the first letter of all the following words

explanation.surface: Cheap wine does not finish off drinkers, so a stronger spirit is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Vodka is a strong distilled spirit, far stronger than table wine.

clue.text: Goes to run amok and wander aimlessly

indicators.note: letters that run amok scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone goes off to go wild and drift about.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb, often stooge about, it is British slang for drifting around with no aim.
explanation.definitionFit: To stooge about is to idle around, a slang synonym for drifting with no purpose.

clue.text: Title for news item -Top teacher found on railway track"

parts.note: the head is the senior teacher of a school
a line is a railway track

explanation.surface: A head teacher found on the railway line makes the news.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints READLINE, but the wordplay builds the real word, the title of a newspaper story.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper story's title is printed in large type above it, the very thing named.

clue.text: Make certain criticism doesn't start

indicators.note: doesn't start means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: censure is strong criticism

explanation.surface: Someone makes sure the criticism never begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to guarantee it happens, a synonym of make certain.

clue.text: A good hand is honest, not bent

explanation.surface: A strong poker hand is honestly dealt.
explanation.walkthrough: In poker, a hand of five cards in sequence ranks fairly high; 'bent' is British slang for corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker it is five cards in sequence; it also means truthful and literally not curved.
